accuracy.reason: Cards 1-3 correctly define name discovery, stub/recursive/authority roles, delegation and typed address/alias records. Cards 4-8 accurately qualify old TTLs, negative and failed answers, health-based steering, diagnosis and DNSSEC versus HTTPS. Reserved teaching names are explicitly illustrative.

evidence.quote: Name discovery and serving the HTTP request are separate steps.

mechanisms.reason: All card mechanisms are traceable: recursive referrals then target-address lookup; independent caches age received TTLs; old NXDOMAIN survives a new record; health policy changes future answers, not open connections; client-side result inspection localizes failures; signature trust chains differ from endpoint authentication.

evidence.quote: The resolver finds the answer; authorities supply records for the zones they serve.

coherence.reason: Given HTTP/HTTPS prerequisites, terminology arrives before use and the eight-card progression builds from lookup to aliasing, change, absence, failover, diagnosis and trust. Inspected resolver diagram assigns referral traversal to recursion and TTL diagram preserves 10:05 old-cache lifetime; shared renderer/CSS previously inspected, not executed.

evidence.quote: A and AAAA supply addresses. CNAME names another record owner to resolve.

decisions.reason: TTL reduction is planned ahead with overlap/monitoring and refresh cost; failover requires healthy reachable west capacity. Diagnosis distinguishes cached old answers from bad authority data and HTTP errors. DNSSEC cannot substitute for HTTPS or access control, avoiding security and recovery promises.

evidence.quote: Plan overlap and observe clients; a TTL edit is not a cache purge.

clarity.reason: Plain definitions and the 300-second/30-second example explain independent lifetime rather than propagation folklore. NXDOMAIN/NODATA/SERVFAIL and DNSSEC/HTTPS boundaries are distinct, with no unexplained mandatory protocol details.

evidence.quote: Distinguish an answer about absence from a failure to obtain an answer.

outcomes.reason: Learner traces stub to recursive root/TLD/domain referrals and authoritative alias then usable A/AAAA target, defines roles/zone/delegation/address families and cache shortcuts, and separates requested hostname discovery from HTTPS path/health. Alias alone is insufficient and can cache separately.

Learner computes ordinary old-answer reuse until 12:59, denies 12:01 forced refresh, lowers TTL before waiting old lifetime and switching, preserves overlap with both destinations monitored, and explains query/dependency cost, connections and serve-stale limits without an invented universal shutdown time.

Learner explains independent negative lifetime unaffected by new 30-second positive TTL, distinguishes name absence from missing AAAA and unresolved SERVFAIL, permits failure caching and avoids inventing its remaining lifetime.

Learner separates health detection/policy from answer selection, explains shared resolver/client reuse prevents HTTP proportions, preserves old answers and open connections, and requires reachable healthy spare west capacity rather than instant migration.

Learner allows cached/open-session success while new discovery fails, checks recursive name/type/error/TTL then authority/delegation, separates connection/HTTPS/application diagnostics and HTTP500, and limits alternate DNS servers to individual failures rather than shared errors.

Learner defines signatures and configured-anchor trust chain validating origin/integrity, excludes encryption and health promises, retains HTTPS encrypted transport and requested-hostname certificate matching through aliases, and preserves application permissions.

sourceChecks.claim: Live Cloudflare DNS explanation separates hostname-to-IP discovery and subsequent HTTP exchange, with cached shortcuts; lesson adds explicit health limitation.
Live Route53 lookup sequence confirms recursive root/TLD/authority steps, delegation caching and final answer returned to client; illustrative reserved hierarchy is clearly qualified.
Live Route53 record reference confirms A/IPv4, AAAA/IPv6 and CNAME name mapping; RFC1034 resolver examples support alias follow-up rather than alias-as-address.
Live RFC8767 explicitly permits stale retention/serving beyond ordinary TTL when refresh fails. Received TTL aging supports old-cache arithmetic and rules out a global cutover guarantee.

Live RFC9520 separates NXDOMAIN/NODATA useful negative answers from resolution failures and requires failure caching; RFC2308 followup assigns negative answers their own lifetime, unaffected by a new positive record.

Live Route53 failover guide explicitly couples configured health checks with changed DNS query answers. Cache reuse and connection independence prevent per-request or instantaneous steering guarantees.

Live RFC1034 resolver/delegation/cache examples support comparing client recursive state with authoritative data; DNS protocol discovery remains separate from later connection and HTTP application response.

Live RFC4033 confirms signed data origin/integrity, trust anchors/chains and no confidentiality. RFC9525 service-identity followup supports matching the requested reference identity separately from DNS discovery.
